column45: A thin ribbon of waterfall drops down a towering rock face into a second, lower cascade, framed by dense evergreen trees.

column3: Sunrise on New Year's Day at Susaki
column4: Susaki hatsu hinode no zu (Toto meisho)
column45: Two women in layered kimono lean into the wind on a grassy bank above the shore, looking across a pale bay where long rays spread from a rising red sun toward a tiny Mount Fuji.
column46: Crowds gathered on the Susaki shore before dawn to greet the year's first sunrise, and Kuniyoshi turns its rays into ruled lines racing across the water.
column48: Christie's lot (Springfield Museums/Raymond A. Bidwell provenance): series Toto meisho, signed Ichiyusai Kuniyoshi ga, publisher Kagaya Kichiemon, horizontal oban. AIC sheet is another impression of the same design.

column45: People walk up a steep street between the long white walls of samurai mansions, among them a woman under a parasol, a man in a straw hat and a porter with a cart.
column46: Kasumigaseki, now the seat of Japan's ministries, was then a slope of feudal lords' mansions, and Kuniyoshi uses Western-style perspective to tip the street toward the sky.
column48: Christie's lot (Bidwell provenance): series Toto meisho, signed Ichiyusai Kuniyoshi ga, publisher Kagaya Kichiemon, horizontal oban. AIC sheet is another impression of the same design. Third Kuniyoshi in dataset (existing 1 + Susaki).

column3: The Cloth-Fulling Jewel River in Settsu Province
column45: Two young women kneel on a wooden floor, one smoothing cloth over a stone block while the other lifts a wooden mallet, beside a barred window with a flowering branch.
column46: Beating cloth on a stone was a stock autumn image in classical poetry, and Harunobu restages the old poem as a quiet chore shared by two fashionable girls.
column48: Christie's lot (Bidwell provenance): untitled series Mutamagawa (Six Jewel Rivers), signed Suzuki Harunobu ga, vertical chuban 27.6 x 20.6 cm. Met 56419 is another impression of the same design.

column3: Burning Maple Leaves to Heat Sake
column45: Three young people kneel around a small brazier heating a kettle over burning red maple leaves, while slanting rain falls past an open veranda onto a maple tree.
column46: The scene quotes a Chinese verse about warming wine with fallen autumn leaves, moved by Harunobu into a rainy Edo room.
column48: Christie's lot title 'Burning maple leaves to heat sake in a rainy day', signed Suzuki Harunobu ga, vertical chuban 27.3 x 21 cm. AIC 20979 (28.7 x 21.6 cm, signed Suzuki Harunobu ga, rain visible) is another impression of the same design. Third Harunobu in dataset (existing 1 + Toi no Tamagawa).

column3: The Actor Ichikawa Ebizo III in a Shibaraku Scene
column45: A kabuki actor with red-striped makeup and enormous checked robes strikes a pose, raising a red signboard in one hand, a long sword thrust through his sash.
column46: In Shibaraku a hero stops a villain with a single shout of 'Wait a moment!', and Shunsho was among the first to give such actors recognisable faces.
column48: Christie's lot: 'The actor Ichikawa Ebizo in Shibaraku', signed Shunsho zu, 11th month 1775, hosoban. Met 36872 (Ebizo III as Shinozuka Iga no kami Sadatsuna in a Shibaraku scene, 11th month 1775) is another impression of the same design.

column45: An elderly shaven-headed man in a dark blue robe kneels on a patterned cushion with prayer beads in his hands, beneath columns of brushed calligraphy.
column46: Issued months after Hiroshige died in the 1858 cholera epidemic, this tribute by his colleague Kunisada carries the landscape master's farewell poem.
column48: Christie's lot: Portrait of Hiroshige, signed Toyokuni ga (Kunisada used the name Toyokuni III), publisher Uoya Eikichi, 9th month 1858, vertical oban. Met 53719 is another impression of the same memorial print.

column4: Kamakura bansho, Tsurugaoka yori Boshu yama no zu (Meisho hakkei)
column45: A high view over a shrine compound of curved roofs, gates and pine trees on a wooded hill, with white sails on the bay and blue mountains beyond.
column46: Toyokuni II, better known for actors, tried his hand at famous-view landscapes just as Hiroshige and Hokusai made travel prints the fashion.
column48: Christie's lot: series Meisho hakkei (Eight famous views), signed Toyokuni hitsu, publisher Iseya Rihei, c. 1833-34, horizontal oban. AIC 47472 (Utagawa Toyoshige/Toyokuni II, same title) is another impression of the same design.

column38: Salon Rose Croix du 10 mars au 10 avril. Galerie Durand-Ruel. affiche, Carlos Schwabe Verdoux, Ducourtioux & Huillard sc..jpg
column45: A tall poster framed by stylised lily columns shows a woman in dark robes reaching toward a pale winged figure on a stair strewn with lilies, a lettered panel below.

Image: BnF/Gallica impression via Commons (PD), same 1892 Draeger poster (engravers Verdoux, Ducourtioux & Huillard). Christie's gives Schwabe's dates as 1866-1928 (Wikidata: d. 1926). GBP 940 = ~USD 1,425 at 2000 FX.

column45: Passengers crowd the bench of a Paris omnibus, drawn in rapid parallel etched lines, a young woman in a dark hat seen in profile at the centre beside the window.

column48: Christie's lot (Armour collection): etching 1892, third (final) state, signed in pencil, from the edition of 75 (A. 72; H. & H. 183). CMA 130909 is a third-state (III/III, Hjert 183) impression of the same plate.

column3: Comtesse Charles d'Agoult and Her Daughter Claire
column14: Graphite heightened with white and touches of yellow watercolour

column38: Hendrick Goltzius, The Fall of Man, 1616, NGA 95659.jpg
